note: Task 9 (chunk e2): the posture call. `startCall`, `scheduleTaps`, `tap`, `choose`, `end` of cards.html, wired to the engine's call (its id, her named postures in her order, her window, her lines) instead of the prototype's panel. The CSS (`#call`, `#callWord`, `#dots`, `#callLine`, `#fan`, `.pc`, `#dimmer`, `#dial.called`) is css/65-call.css; the shots (`npm run shots -- cards`) compare the moment. `tapTimes` and `fanPlace` are the numbers of `scheduleTaps` and `startCall` as functions of their own (tests/ui/instruments/call.test.ts). Declared beyond the five functions: (1) review I1, the stop word: the prototype's fan lies over its `#stopPill`; P15a's "the stop word always ends a hold" outranks that geometry, so while a call is drawn the scene lifts the pill's host into the moment layer above the call (`.alius-stop-lift`, z 9, at the place it had; sceneScreen `placeStop`, back when the call is gone through `onGone`), and an answered call's cards take no pointer (`.alius-call[data-outcome] .alius-call-card`); `npm run test:layout` checks the pill is clickable in the `callhold` fixture. (2) Readable mode: the call's cards are opaque and unblurred (P10's readable rule; the prototype has no readable form for the call).

differences.reason: Wiring: the engine's call (`o`: its id, the called posture and her name for it, her named postures in her order that pass `entryAllowed`, her window, reduced motion, her accent and hand) replaces the prototype's panel (`S`, `NAMED.slice(0, 4)`, a random pick: the engine picks by `practiceRoll`); the elements are the call's own (`build`), the dim lives under the scene's UI (`o.dim`) and the ring on the scene's dial (`o.dial`); each card is a button (`data-posture-choice`, `data-call`, `data-analyze`) holding the dial's mannequin (`mannequinSvg(poseOf(base))`, as the prototype's build does), placed by `fanPlace` (the prototype's numbers); a hover does not move a card once the call is answered; timers go through `o.schedule` so `cancelCall` stops them; `is-writing` is the prototype's `write` class; the log line is prototype only.

Wiring: the answer goes to the engine at once (`o.take`: the posture chosen, none for the last tap, late when the window had passed), and her line is card-voice.md §5 by her style through `voiceLine` (`o.line`); the dial takes the posture from the state (the scene redraws it 380 ms after the answer, at once with reduced motion), so `drawDial` is not called here and a void answer (R9) leaves it as it is; `is-right` / `is-wrong` / `is-writing` are the prototype's `right` / `wrongpick` / `write`; every timer goes through `o.schedule` and the last one tears the moment down (`teardown`) so nothing stays; the outcome is marked on the root (`data-outcome`) for the shots and the tests.
